tasks.title: Let a worker declare its cost basis in workers.json (worker_cost_basis_is_declared_and_defaults_to_neutral)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn worker_cost_basis_is_declared_and_defaults_to_neutral' tests/contract_config.rs && openspec validate --specs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL: a campaign can DECLARE how expensive each worker is, so cost estimation works even though no provider reports a price. Two optional fields on `Worker` in src/config.rs:

    /// Model size in BILLIONS of parameters - an operator-declared PROXY for
    /// expense, used when the provider reports no price. Absent = neutral
    /// (no opinion), so an existing workers.json keeps working unchanged.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub params_b: Option<f64>,
    /// Real price in USD per MILLION tokens, when the operator knows it.
    /// A declared price beats the `params_b` proxy.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub price_per_mtok_usd: Option<f64>,

Document in those doc comments that these are DECLARED assumptions, not vendor data: agentflow never guesses a model's size from its name.

LOAD-TIME VALIDATION (in the existing `fn validate(tasks, workers)` in src/config.rs, around line 249 - it returns `Result<Vec<String>, String>` where Ok is the warnings and Err is a fatal message that makes `af` exit 2):
1. A declared value that is not usable (not finite, or <= 0) is a CONFIG ERROR naming the worker and the field, e.g. `worker "zai": params_b must be a finite positive number`. Use `crate::cost::is_usable` - src/cost.rs already exists by the time you start, read its real signature. A NaN weight would silently defeat cost comparison, which is why this is an error and not a warning.
2. A worker that declares NEITHER value gets a WARNING (not an error): `worker "zai" has no cost basis (params_b or price_per_mtok_usd): cost estimates will be neutral for it`. One warning per such worker, so `af validate`'s existing `N warning(s)` count reflects it. Only warn for ENABLED workers - a disabled worker is not dispatched.

The `Worker` struct is built with STRUCT LITERALS in SEVEN places and every one stops compiling the moment you add a field, so update ALL of them (set the new fields to their defaults at each): `src/config.rs` (`impl Default for Worker`, ~line 128), `src/execute.rs` (~line 664 and ~line 866), `src/router.rs` (~line 65, in-module test), `tests/contract_prompt.rs` (~line 34), `tests/contract_env.rs` (~line 129), `tests/cli.rs` (~line 1045). Every one of those files is in your declared scope - do not drop a field to stay narrow, and do not edit any file that is NOT in your scope.

TESTS in tests/contract_config.rs (the file already covers the worker schema - follow its existing style):
1. `fn worker_cost_basis_is_declared_and_defaults_to_neutral()` - parse a workers.json with both fields set on one worker and NEITHER on another; assert the values survive and that the second worker defaults to `None`/`None` (neutral). Prove an OLD workers.json that never mentions the fields still loads unchanged.
2. A test for the rejection path: a non-finite (or <= 0) `params_b`/`price_per_mtok_usd` fails validation with a message naming the worker and field.
3. A test for the warning path: a worker with no declared basis appears in the warnings, and a fully-declared worker does not.

TRACEABILITY: this extends the worker schema, so update the `Worker schema loading` requirement in `openspec/specs/config/spec.md`. A `## MODIFIED Requirements` block is a FULL REPLACEMENT, not a patch: reproduce EVERY surviving scenario VERBATIM or it is silently deleted. Put the `// spec: config/<req>#<scenario>` marker on your own test in tests/contract_config.rs. `cargo test --test spec_traceability` must stay green and the allowlist in tests/spec_traceability.rs must stay EMPTY. Finish by running `openspec validate --specs` (7/7 must pass).
README: document both fields in the workers.json reference, and say plainly that they are the operator's declaration used only when the provider reports no price.
DO NOT BREAK: the existing `tests/contract_config.rs` tests, the worker defaults, `validate`'s warning ORDER for its existing warnings, and `tests/cli.rs`.

tasks.title: Make af cost show estimated expense when no provider reports a price (cost_report_shows_relative_expense_when_no_provider_reports_a_price)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn cost_report_shows_relative_expense_when_no_provider_reports_a_price' tests/cli.rs && openspec validate --specs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL: `af cost` must answer "which worker is burning my budget?" even though every provider here reports `cost.total` = 0. It shows the tokens it already records (round 9) PLUS an EXPENSE estimate derived from the basis each worker declares (the other two tasks in this campaign added `Worker.params_b` / `Worker.price_per_mtok_usd` and `src/cost.rs` - read both before you start).

EXACT OUTPUT CONTRACT (follow it literally; it is asserted by the gate):
1. Add a `COST` column to BOTH tables in `run::cost` (src/run.rs, `pub fn cost(cfg, st, filter)` around line 1109): in the TASK table immediately AFTER `TOKENS`, in the WORKER table immediately after `TRUST`. Keep every existing column and the existing column order otherwise.
2. Per row, the cell is:
   - `$<usd>` when that worker declares `price_per_mtok_usd`: use `cost::estimate_usd(tokens, price)` from src/cost.rs, formatted with 4 decimals (e.g. `$0.0123`). This is REAL money.
   - `N.NNx` when it declares only `params_b`: the RATE ratio from `cost::size_ratio(params_b, all_declared)`, formatted with 2 decimals and a literal `x` suffix (e.g. `1.25x`). `all_declared` is the list of `cost::basis(..)` for EVERY worker in `cfg.workers`; doc-comment that the cheapest declaring worker is therefore always exactly `1.00x`. This is a PROXY, so it must never be printed with a `$`.
   - `-` when the row's worker declares neither, or when a receipt names a worker that is not in `cfg.workers` at all.
   - A TASK row can span several attempts on different workers: SUM the dollars when EVERY attempt in the row is `Priced`; use the TOKEN-WEIGHTED MEAN ratio when EVERY attempt is `Sized` (sum over attempts of tokens*ratio, divided by summed tokens); otherwise `-`. A row with no tokens is `-`.
3. Print ONE basis line ABOVE the tables, stating the rule so a proxy can never be misread as money. Exactly one of:
   - `cost basis: declared prices (USD per 1M tokens)`
   - `cost basis: params_b proxy (relative; cheapest declared worker = 1.00x)`
   - `cost basis: none (no worker declares params_b or price_per_mtok_usd)`
   Choose it from `cfg.workers`: prices if ANY worker declares a price, else the proxy if any declares params_b, else none. When BOTH kinds are declared, some rows are `$` and some are `N.NNx` - say so on the basis line (e.g. append `; some workers declare only params_b`).
4. If any receipt names a worker absent from `cfg.workers`, print ONE footnote line after the tables listing those names (sorted, deduped): `note: N attempt(s) name a worker absent from the config, shown as '-': foo, bar`. This is normal - historical receipts outlive config edits - so it must NEVER be an error and must never block the report.
5. `-` (the placeholder) must also be used for rows whose receipts carry no `tokens` (legacy receipts), so a report over old data still renders.

TESTS - extend tests/cli.rs (it already has the cost-report tests, including `cost_report_surfaces_wasted_spend`; follow that style, which builds a `Cli` fixture and writes receipts through `Store::append_receipt`):
1. `fn cost_report_shows_relative_expense_when_no_provider_reports_a_price()` - two workers declaring different `params_b`, receipts carrying `tokens`; assert the basis line says `params_b proxy`, that the cheapest declaring worker shows `1.00x`, the bigger one shows its real ratio, and that the placeholder `-` appears for an attempt whose receipt has `tokens: None`.
2. A test that a DECLARED PRICE wins: a worker with `price_per_mtok_usd` shows `$<usd>` computed from its tokens, and never a `x` ratio.
3. A test for the footnote: a receipt naming an unknown worker yields the `note: ...` line, shows `-`, and does NOT make `af cost` fail.

TRACEABILITY: this changes user-visible `af cost` output, so update the `Cost report` requirement in `openspec/specs/cli/spec.md` (a `## MODIFIED Requirements` block is a FULL REPLACEMENT - reproduce every surviving scenario VERBATIM) and mark your tests `// spec: cli/<req>#<scenario>`. `cargo test --test spec_traceability` must stay green, the allowlist must stay EMPTY, and `openspec validate --specs` must be 7/7.
README: document the new column and the basis line under the cost-report section.
DO NOT BREAK: the round-6 `--last`/`--since`/`--task` narrowing, round 9's `warning: unreadable receipt ...` line and WASTED BY REASON cause grouping, the TOKENS column, and `run::status_board`.

OTHER FILES THAT PIN THE TABLE SHAPE - they are IN YOUR SCOPE precisely because a new column must be reflected there, and a first attempt failed for editing one of them without permission. Update them deliberately and say so in your summary:
- `tests/ledger_truth.rs` asserts the TASK row format verbatim (`format!("{:<12} {:<9} {:<10.1} {:<9} {}", "A", 2, 3.0, "350", "m")` around lines 235 and 242, plus the header assertion around line 230). Those strings MUST gain the new column or the suite fails - fix them and keep the tests' INTENT (tokens summed, `-` when absent).
- `tests/interrupted.rs` asserts WORKER rows (`format!("{:<14} {:<11} {:.2}", ...)`, around lines 147 and 209). Its point is that an interrupted attempt stays out of WINS/TOTAL - keep that meaning intact.
- `src/run.rs`'s own in-module tests (around lines 1932, 1950, 1956, 1966, 1970, 2041, 2069) assert row shapes too.
Adding a column IS an intentional shape change; where an assertion pins the old shape, update it rather than weakening it to a bare `contains("A")`.

tasks.title: Prefer the cheaper worker only when trust ties, never overriding measured trust (the_router_prefers_the_cheaper_worker_only_when_trust_ties)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn the_router_prefers_the_cheaper_worker_only_when_trust_ties' tests/contract_scheduler.rs && openspec validate --specs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL: make the declared cost basis (from `Worker.params_b` / `Worker.price_per_mtok_usd`, see src/config.rs) actually influence dispatch - but ONLY as a tie-break, never as a primary score. Rationale you must preserve and comment: measured reliability must always outrank a declared expense assumption, and cost-per-task is confounded by task difficulty (hard tasks need the big model), so a cost term in the score itself would penalise a worker for being given the hard work and would starve it - a self-reinforcing bias.

WHERE: `Router::pick` in src/router.rs (~line 20). It currently computes, per eligible worker, `score = mean + explore` (UCB1) and keeps the FIRST maximum because the comparison is strictly greater, so an exact tie is resolved by CONFIG ORDER by accident.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR:
1. A STRICTLY HIGHER score still always wins. Never let a cheaper worker displace a worker with a measurably better score - add a test that proves this, it is the most important property here.
2. When a candidate's score TIES the current best within a small tolerance (use 1e-9 and define it as a named constant with a comment explaining it is a tie tolerance, not a tuning knob), keep whichever of the two is CHEAPER, using `crate::cost::compare(crate::cost::basis(w.params_b, w.price_per_mtok_usd), <the incumbent's basis>)` from src/cost.rs. Only `Some(Ordering::Less)` may replace the incumbent.
3. Bases that are NOT comparable - one worker priced, the other only sized, or either declaring nothing - must NEVER trigger a swap. `cost::compare` already returns `None` for those; do not invent a conversion between a price and a parameter count. Config order remains the final tie-break.
4. Keep the function's signature and its "no eligible worker -> None" behaviour unchanged, and keep it allocation-free.

TESTS in tests/contract_scheduler.rs (it already builds `Router`s and `Worker`s for the scheduler contract tests - follow that style):
1. `fn the_router_prefers_the_cheaper_worker_only_when_trust_ties()` - two workers with IDENTICAL stats where score ties: the one declaring the smaller `params_b` is picked regardless of config order (write it so the CHEAPER worker is NOT first in the list, or the test passes by accident).
2. A test proving a strictly better trust score beats a cheaper competitor (an expensive worker with a better win rate is still chosen).
3. A test that an incomparable pair (one priced, one sized) keeps config order, and that two workers declaring nothing keep config order.

TRACEABILITY: this changes dispatch behaviour, so update the `scheduling` spec (openspec/specs/scheduling/spec.md) with the tie-break - a `## MODIFIED Requirements` block is a FULL REPLACEMENT, so reproduce every surviving scenario VERBATIM - and mark your tests `// spec: scheduling/<req>#<scenario>`. Note: round 9 added the requirement covering the task-level `priority` tie-break; keep it intact and add the worker-level cost tie-break as its own scenario. `cargo test --test spec_traceability` must stay green, the allowlist must stay EMPTY, and `openspec validate --specs` must be 7/7.
DO NOT BREAK: the existing in-module tests in src/router.rs (including the `Worker` literal at ~line 65 - you may need to add the two new fields there, set to `None`), `tests/contract_scheduler.rs`'s existing scope/priority tests, and `pick`'s existing UCB1 arithmetic for non-tied scores.
